title: New DB migration scripts disable TLS cert validation by default
description: Both db-migrate-023.mjs and db-migrate-024.mjs build the pg client with `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: rejectUnauthorized ?? false }` for any non-local database URL. Because the default is false when POSTGRES_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED is unset, the scripts will accept any TLS certificate for remote connections. This weakens transport security for migrations and allows a network-adjacent attacker to intercept credentials or alter migration traffic if they can position themselves in the connection path. A secure default should enforce certificate validation and only relax it when explicitly configured.

title: Postgres init retries with TLS verification disabled
description: The commit adds a fallback path for Postgres initialization that detects SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN errors and reattempts the connection with TLS certificate verification disabled. Because this fallback is enabled by default unless an operator explicitly configures POSTGRES_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED or disables POSTGRES_SSL_ALLOW_SELF_SIGNED_FALLBACK, a network-adjacent attacker who can intercept traffic can force a self-signed certificate error and then MITM the database connection. This exposes database credentials and allows read/modify access to backend data.

title: Rate-limit revert can block LayerZero VRF inbound lane
description: CreatorVRFConsumerV2_5 now reverts when `_consumeRateLimit` returns false in `_lzReceive`. LayerZero OApp delivery is typically blocking on failed inbound messages, so a single rate-limited request can leave the inbound lane stuck until a manual retry after the window resets. If remote chain requesters are permissionless, an attacker can spam requests to hit the limit and halt all subsequent VRF processing from that chain. Previously, the code simply returned (ignored) on rate limit without reverting, avoiding inbound lane blockage.

title: Cursor install script executes remote Foundry installer unsafely
description: The commit adds .cursor/environment.json that tells the Cursor cloud agent to run .cursor/install.sh during provisioning. The install script downloads and executes https://foundry.paradigm.xyz directly via `curl | bash` without signature or checksum validation. If the download is compromised (MITM, DNS hijack, or upstream compromise), arbitrary code executes in the agent environment, which can expose secrets or alter builds. This is a supply-chain RCE risk introduced by the new automation.

title: Solana transfer hook allows forged lottery entries
description: The new `transfer_hook` instruction accepts all token accounts as `UncheckedAccount` and never verifies that the source/destination accounts are Token-2022 accounts for the provided mint or that the call originated from a real Token-2022 transfer. The handler simply reads raw bytes from these unverified accounts and uses the extracted owner to decide whether to record a lottery entry. Because anyone can call this instruction directly (or via the fallback) and supply arbitrary accounts with crafted data, an attacker can fabricate a source account whose owner matches an allow‑listed AMM program and force `PendingEntries` to record entries without performing a swap. This allows lottery entry stuffing, skewing win chances and potentially draining jackpots once the keeper relays the forged entries to Base.

title: CSW link points can be farmed with unlimited addresses
description: The commit introduces /waitlist/csw-link, which awards CSW link points using the provided CSW address as the ledger source_id. The points ledger is only idempotent per (signup_id, source, source_id). Because source_id is the CSW address, a caller can repeatedly submit different addresses for the same email to insert new rows and accrue unlimited 250‑point awards. There is no check for an existing CSW link, nor is the CSW address persisted for uniqueness enforcement, so this can be exploited to manipulate waitlist rankings or allocations.

title: Public authStatus endpoint leaks masked Zora server API key
description: The commit adds `/api/zora/cli/authStatus`, implemented as a read-only GET endpoint that explicitly disables the server-key requirement and returns the result of `authStatusCli()`. That helper reads `process.env.ZORA_SERVER_API_KEY` and returns a masked version (first 8 and last 4 characters). Although partially masked, this leaks secret material and confirms the presence of the server key to unauthenticated users, which can aid targeted abuse or key-guessing/social engineering. The endpoint should avoid returning any portion of the key or should be protected by authentication/allowlist.

title: Browser defaults skip Zora migration trust checks
description: The commit introduces a browser-only gate (VERIFY_MIGRATION_IMPLEMENTATION) that defaults to false unless an environment flag is explicitly set. When false, the migration scanner skips verifying contract bytecode against the allowlist and unconditionally marks all LiquidityMigrated log emitters as trusted. Since any contract can emit the same event topic with self-referential pool keys, an attacker can spoof migration events to have arbitrary coins flagged as migrated, causing the UI to display lower (1%) fees and “migrated” status for untrusted assets. This is an integrity issue that can mislead users and affect trading decisions.

title: Wallet-gated AI prompts no longer enforced
description: generateLlmResponse previously required a valid sender wallet for non-explicit prompts, which is how /ai commands are passed in from handleKeeprCommand after stripping the prefix. The refactor removed this check and now proceeds with runtime/LLM execution even when toSenderAddress returns null or a fallback ZERO_ADDRESS. As a result, unlinked users can invoke /ai and receive full AI responses, potentially exhausting the LLM budget or bypassing intended access controls for chat AI usage.

title: Unauthenticated Uniswap Trading API proxy exposes server key
description: The commit adds multiple /api/uniswap/* handlers that accept arbitrary requests, apply only IP-based rate limiting, and forward them to the Uniswap Trading API using the server-side API key. Because there is no session or authorization check, any external caller can use these endpoints as an open proxy to the Trading API (including plan creation/update). This can lead to API key abuse, quota exhaustion, and unauthorized manipulation of cross-chain plan state tied to the project’s API key.

title: AdminOps accepts insecure HTTP agentURI values
description: AdminOps uses isContentAddressedAgentUri to gate agent URI registration and updates. The commit expands accepted schemes to include http:// and https:// without enforcing content-addressed or HTTPS-only gateway constraints. This allows on-chain agent registrations to point at mutable or plaintext URLs, which can be altered or intercepted to change agent metadata after registration, potentially misleading validators or users who rely on that metadata.

title: Keepr join lock not enforced allows joins during lock
description: Keepr introduces a join lock (joinLocked) that owners can toggle via commands, but the join API and background join-request processor never check this flag. As a result, any eligible user (or any user when gating is disabled) can still enqueue an XMTP add_member action even after the owner has locked joins. This bypasses the intended access control for pausing membership changes.

title: XMTP init blocked when OPFS check fails
description: The commit adds a guard that refuses to create a new XMTP installation whenever a local OPFS database is detected but Client.build fails. However, hasOpfsDatabase() intentionally returns true on OPFS errors or lack of support (“assume DB might exist”). In environments where OPFS is unsupported or temporarily fails, the code now treats this as an existing DB, attempts Client.build, and then returns an error instead of falling through to Client.create. This regression can block chat initialization entirely until users clear storage or use a different browser, representing an availability bug introduced by the new logic.

title: BigInt buffer conversion truncates most-significant bytes
description: The newly vendored bigint-buffer implementation enforces the output width by slicing the hex string from the start. When a BigInt exceeds the requested width, this drops the least‑significant bytes and keeps the most‑significant bytes. That behavior silently corrupts the encoded value (e.g., 0x1234 with width=1 becomes 0x12 instead of 0x34 or throwing), which can lead to incorrect serialization of amounts or IDs in any consumer of this library.

title: Mobile chat overlay ignores disconnect state
description: The reverted change removes the isConnected gate and dependency from the mobile overlay useEffect in ChatWidget. When a user disconnects while a chat window or bar is open, the component returns null (chat UI disappears) but the effect no longer re-runs to dispatch an inactive overlay event. Layout listens for that event to hide the mobile nav, so the nav can remain hidden with no way to reopen the chat, effectively stranding users on mobile until refresh.

title: Direct executeBatch fallback treats reverted tx as success
description: The commit adds a direct owner EOA executeBatch fallback. After sending the transaction it only calls waitForTransactionReceipt and immediately persists a successful result without checking the receipt status. In viem, waitForTransactionReceipt resolves even when the transaction reverted. This means a failed executeBatch can still be marked as successful, causing subsequent phases to run against an incomplete or failed deployment and misleading users about the actual on-chain state.

title: Root entrypoint chown enables symlink-based privilege escalation
description: The Dockerfile change removes the non-root USER and introduces a root-run entrypoint that executes `chown -R node:node /data/.xmtp-data` before dropping privileges. Recursive chown follows symlinks by default. If an attacker can write to the mounted XMTP volume (e.g., via a prior compromise or a shared volume), they can place a symlink inside `/data/.xmtp-data` pointing to sensitive locations such as `/etc` or `/app`. On the next restart, the root chown will change ownership of those targets to the unprivileged node user, enabling modification of system or application files and potential privilege escalation/persistence inside the container. This behavior did not exist prior to the commit because the container ran as node and the chown was done at build time.

title: Preflight simulation blocks batch deploys on Unauthorized
description: simulateSmartWalletCalls only ignores Unauthorized when a direct-call simulation succeeded, but direct-call simulation is only performed for single-call batches. For multi-call phases it simulates executeBatch from the smart wallet, which commonly reverts with Unauthorized because it is not called from EntryPoint. DeployVault now always runs this preflight simulation and throws on any errorName, so multi-call phases (approvals + deploy/finalize) can be blocked even though the real ERC‑4337 flow would succeed.

title: Deploy flow regression for multi-owner Coinbase Smart Wallets
description: The refactor removed the Privy smart-wallet path and always routes deployments through sendCoinbaseSmartWalletUserOperation. When users connect directly with a Coinbase Smart Wallet, the connected address equals the smart wallet contract. The helper enforces that ownerAddress is an onchain owner and throws if it cannot find that owner unless there is only one owner. This means multi-owner smart wallets connected directly via wagmi can no longer deploy, which is a regression compared to the previous Privy smart-wallet path.
